summary: Discovery focused on latency and throughput requirements for a customer-facing chat assistant; discussed p95 SLOs, concurrency, streaming tokens/sec, and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Agreed to run a POC benchmark with sample prompts and to share pricing and security docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Jenna: ok thanks everyone for joining, we'll kick off — i'm jennapark from Redwood, with marco our se. thanks priya for coordinating.
[00:12] Priya: yeah hi, thanks. we're trying to understand whether we go hosted or dedicated, main constraints are p95 latency under load and throughput for concurrent users, also data residency and KMS.
[00:24] Marco: great; can you give a sense of current traffic pattern and target p95?
[00:30] Priya: sure — peak concurrent active users about 3k sessions, roughly 12 requests per second at the peak, average response length 60 tokens but bursty to 200 tokens for some flows. p95 needs to be sub 400ms for initial token, and end-to-end under 1.2s ideally.
[00:48] Daniel: and we stream tokens to the client; so steady tokens/sec matters. We see about 500 tokens/sec aggregate and want to scale to 2k tokens/sec.
[00:58] Marco: ok that helps. when you say sub 400ms p95, is that for first-token latency or for full generation?
[01:05] Priya: first-token p95 is what product cares about for perceived snappiness. full generation can be higher, but we'd like to keep interactive flows under 1.2s.
[01:14] Jenna: noted. our Hosted API can hit low first-token p95 for smaller models, but with larger open models we often point customers to Dedicated for predictable tail latency at scale.
[01:25] Priya: what does predictable mean — we saw huge variance in our current infra because of co-tenancy and autotuning.
[01:32] Marco: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, you get predictable throughput and less noisy neighbors; plus you can enable fixed batching and KV cache sizing. We can provision for your concurrency target.
[01:44] Sofia: question on streaming — when you stream, do you batch tokens across concurrent streams? we worry about per-session latency increasing.
[01:52] Marco: yes streaming interacts with batching. Our runtime supports continuous batching with priority routing — small streams can be flushed quickly. There's a tradeoff: aggressive batching improves throughput (tokens/sec) but can hurt first-token p95. We can tune batch windows per route.
[02:08] Priya: can you give example numbers?
[02:11] Marco: e.g., on A100-equivalent nodes with an optimized 7B model, we see first-token p95 ~120-180ms at low concurrency, at 3k concurrent sessions with Dedicated we can keep first-token p95 under 300-350ms depending on batch target. For 13B models that rises, 7-9x higher token compute; tokens/sec per GPU will drop.
[02:34] Daniel: that's useful. For our workload we were thinking 13B quantized to 4-bit to save cost — does Redwood support quantized model variants and automatic fallback?
[02:44] Marco: yes we support quantized variants and model catalog routing; you can pin model versions and we have automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants if capacity constrained. The runtime is quantization-friendly.
[02:55] Priya: about benchmarks — what would you need from us to run a realistic throughput run?
[02:59] Marco: sample prompts, distribution of response lengths, concurrency matrix (like 100/500/1k/3k concurrent schedules), whether streaming is enabled, and expected token/sec per session. We'll run a sweep and report p50/p95/p99 for first-token and overall latency, plus tokens/sec and GPU utilization.
[03:15] Priya: okay we'll share prompts and a small dataset.
[03:18] Jenna: also want to highlight routing — for cost control you can route low-priority traffic to a cheaper model or region; that often hits the cost/latency balance you described.
[03:27] Priya: can we get an estimate for unit economics? like cost per 1M tokens at your hosted tier vs dedicated reserved?
[03:33] Jenna: yes i'll send ballpark numbers, but dedicated pricing depends on commit and instance type. We'll include example numbers for your concurrency and throughput profile.
[03:40] Sofia: security checklist — do you have SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS support, and audit logs?
[03:46] Marco: yes SOC2, SAML/SSO, and we can integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM on Private deployments; Dedicated has at-rest encryption and customer keys for some options. We'll share the security whitepaper.
[03:58] Daniel: will we be able to run the benchmark in our VPC or is it on Redwood infra?
[04:03] Marco: for POC we can run either — Hosted POC runs on our infra; for Private we can do an on-prem or VPC installation but that takes longer. For initial bench, Hosted or Dedicated with VPN peering usually suffices.
[04:15] Priya: timeline — we want to decide by end of July. Possible to have POC results by mid-July?
[04:20] Jenna: yes if we get prompts and access by next week we can run benchmarks and have results in 10 business days, pushing into mid-July.
[04:28] Priya: perfect.
[04:30] Marco: quick note on metrics we'll deliver: first-token p50/p95/p99, end-to-end latency, tokens/sec aggregate, GPU utilization, and recommended batch/caching config.
[04:42] Priya: one more — do you support function calling and structured output streaming? we need partial responses.
[04:48] Marco: yes we support streaming structured outputs and function/tool calling; can configure streaming chunk sizes. Smaller chunks = better interactivity but more overhead.
[04:58] Daniel: any customers with similar scale?
[05:01] Jenna: we've onboarded a couple of mid-market SaaS with 1-5k concurrent sessions; I can share a redacted case study.
[05:09] Sofia: about tail latency — do you have SLO tools to alert when p95 drifts?
[05:13] Marco: yes Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, regression alerts tied to prompt sets, and automated fallback policies to route to smaller models or degrade gracefully.
[05:23] Priya: Great. let's talk failure modes — if a GPU node goes down, how do you keep requests online?
[05:29] Marco: we have smart routing and automatic fallback; for Dedicated we can configure burst to other pools or to Hosted. For Private, HA depends on customer infra but we provide guidance.
[05:40] Priya: any limits on concurrency per instance?
[05:44] Marco: throughput is function of instance type and model; we'll model it in the runbook. We'll also show tokens/sec per GPU and estimate number of GPUs for steady-state and peak.
[05:55] Jenna: ok quick recap of action items and next steps — we'll send pricing and security docs, Marco will share benchmark runbook, LumenTech will provide prompts and concurrency matrix. schedule poc kick-off for week of 7/6.
[06:08] Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:10] Jenna: thanks, we'll follow up via email.
[47:35] [end recording — longer silence/meeting wrap, some cross talk omitted]
Note: transcript contains minor transcription errors (model names sometimes misrecognized, e.g., "K V cache" vs KV cache).
